claims.text: Machine-learning corrections integrated into defect-inclusive analytical models can significantly improve thermal-conductivity predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed approach can significantly improve electrical-conductivity predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed accuracy improvement applies in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
The initial bulk HfNbTaTiZr material is as-cast and multiphase.
The initial material contains inherent crystal defects.
Some HfNbTaTiZr specimens contain 1 wt.% oxygen.
The predictive workflow explicitly represents lattice imperfections, impurity effects, and defect-induced scattering.
Quantum and phonon-scattering anomalies predominate in HfNbTaTiZr between 0 and 200 K.
Phonon-phonon interactions and impurity scattering, notably from oxygen, influence conductivity between 300 and 1200 K.
Defects and oxygen impurities alter local bonding environments in HfNbTaTiZr.
Defects and oxygen impurities alter phonon dispersion in HfNbTaTiZr.
The correction framework can quantitatively capture defect- and oxygen-induced changes in local bonding and phonon dispersion.
Empirical data on oxygen content and defect distributions can be used to correct scattering rates, electron-phonon interactions, and anharmonic lattice dynamics.
Standard analytical models neglect relevant deviations in scattering rates, electron-phonon interactions, and anharmonic lattice dynamics.
Accounting for these effects will yield a more realistic representation of temperature-dependent scattering and conductivity trends.
The proposed predictions will closely match conductivity measurements and have significantly lower errors than perfect-crystal predictions in both temperature windows.
Defect-free analytical predictions systematically under- or overestimate conductivity because they neglect defect and oxygen-impurity scattering.
The enhanced accuracy is expected to apply to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing up to approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Predictive accuracy may deteriorate above approximately 1 wt.% oxygen or outside the specified temperature windows.
